**`LiveRegion.tsx`:**
- `role="status"` is hardcoded regardless of the `politeness` prop. `role="status"` carries an implicit `aria-live="polite"`, so rendering it alongside `aria-live="assertive"` sends conflicting signals to screen readers. For assertive announcements, `role="alert"` should be used.
- The JSDoc on `useAnnouncer` (line 79) says "Cleans up the announcer on unmount" — but no cleanup function is returned from any `useEffect`. This is both an incorrect comment and a real resource leak.
- `useState` is used to create a stable function reference (line 99), which is non-idiomatic. `useCallback` is the standard hook for this pattern.
- `{...rest}` is spread *after* the hardcoded `role`, `aria-live`, and `aria-atomic` attributes, meaning those can be silently overridden by callers. The `politeness` prop is destructured, so callers can't use it AND `aria-live` to conflict — but `role` and `aria-atomic` are vulnerable.

**`toHaveLiveRegion.ts`:**
- Line 20 JSDoc says "string for exact match" but the code uses `content.includes(text)`, which is a substring match. Documentation and implementation are inconsistent.

**`LiveRegion.test.tsx`:**
- `expect(el).toBeDefined()` should be `expect(el).toBeInTheDocument()` — the project's jest-dom conventions prefer DOM-specific matchers for DOM assertions.
- `it('fails when no matching live region is found')` — "fails" sounds like the test itself is expected to fail; "throws when no matching live region is found" is clearer.

**`LiveRegion.stories.tsx`:**
- `args: {}` in `PolitenessToggle` is redundant.

**`code/core/src/components/index.ts`:**
- `toHaveLiveRegion` and `LiveRegionMatcherOptions` are test-only utilities being exported from the production components barrel. Per project rules, test utilities should live under a `test-utils/` path.

**General:**
- PR description mentions `extend-to-be-announced` registration in `storybook.setup.ts` and `TestProviderRender` announcement stories — neither appears in the diff. If this is meant to be a follow-up PR, the description is misleading; if it's required for completeness, pieces are missing.
- Two overlapping announcement mechanisms are exported: the declarative `<LiveRegion>` (renders into the React tree) and the imperative `announce()` (injects into `document.body` via `@react-aria/live-announcer`). Using both for the same event triggers double announcements. Documentation should guide consumers on which to use and when.
